entries.title: Expanding Mycelium Web in Soil Layers
entries.description: A central fungal node grows translucent branching tubes through layered soil blocks, with hyphae that split, merge, wrap around pebbles, and leave faint trails as nutrients (colored spheres) flow along glowing segments.

entries.title: Tree–Fungus Nutrient Trading Network
entries.description: Several tree trunks stand stationary while a semi-transparent fungal web expands underground between their roots, transferring colored nutrient particles back and forth along pulsing filaments and updating floating “carbon” and “nitrogen” meters above each tree.

entries.title: Spore Rain and Network Colonization
entries.description: Spores fall like tiny bouncing particles from a mushroom cap onto a flat substrate, where each landing spore sprouts branching hyphae that grow outward, collide, fuse, or repel when different-colored species meet, with labels showing colony boundaries.

entries.title: Competing Fungal Species in a 3D Log
entries.description: A 3D log cross-section is filled by two or three differently colored fungal networks that grow, collide, overtake, or dissolve each other’s filaments, with a transparent cutaway view and a time slider bar showing territory percentage for each species.
